entries.rationale: Exact equality to the Re-CTM 0.3.0 directory and hidden dispatch is an intentionally retired requirement. The Rust shadow executable was already removed. Current catalog, OAuth, MCP and HTTP behavior have independent Rust tests; old 44-record parity and resource measurements remain immutable historical evidence, not new-contract claims. Browser/socket/target coverage is not claimed by this deletion.

This Python shadow exists only for the retired cross-language gateway comparison. No live product behavior depends on it. Authentication tests now use the real Rust router and disposable OAuth stores; no authority-bypass principal constructor replaces this runner. Historical source is recoverable from the pinned baseline.

The one-refresh test/client helper has no remaining product caller. Rust test-only recovery preserves same-envelope, same-run/domain, unchanged-contract and zero-write binding, no uncertain-transport replay and the two-request ceiling. This is not a new SDK or automatic web-model behavior. Real disposable-binary tests use the Rust client; historical target-specific checker interfaces remain separately retained.

Python recovery assertions move beside the Rust test-only helper: one normal call, one fresh retry, cross-run/domain/state/contract denial, no retained/unknown writes replay, revoked-token denial, stale preparer prevention and redacted errors. New negative cases include missing contract fields, fractional counts and uncertain transport; the actual built-binary regression separately checks 500 distinct submissions and restart behavior.

Current pure-policy tests no longer require a sibling Re-CTM checkout, Python oracle, old output hash or cross-language resource measurements. All 135 inputs across 14 groups have independent Rust expectations and actual CLI boundary tests. The inherited fractional minimum bypass is explicitly corrected by df6660c rather than frozen. Historical golden hash and A5 measurements remain unchanged; this deletion does not assert new performance or target qualification.

The 135 named input cases are maintained as package-local Rust test data, with explicit expected results, group-count checks and the recorded 13719-byte input length. No fixture generator or Python execution is needed; command-looking strings are only pure-policy inputs, not commands to execute.

This adapter imports the retired reference project's pure policy functions and has no remaining current caller. Explicit Rust test expectations replace the oracle dependency. Success results and error code/category/retryability/details are checked; exact old Python diagnostic wording is not a new contract. Existing historical reference hashes are preserved, not re-evaluated from the new implementation.

The built Rust CLI is tested directly with empty inherited environment and PATH: all 135 inputs, single/batch equivalence, 1000/1001-item and 1 MiB input limits, malformed JSON/UTF-8, deterministic output and ordered per-item errors. The disposable working directory remains empty. Python batch execution is unnecessary; this is not a browser, Native or entire-host-without-Python claim.

cargo xtask records now owns required governance/iteration/evidence/validation layout, naming, root JSON prohibition, one-to-one relocation kinds and historical hashes. Independent filesystem tests add symlink/path/size guards, new observation seals and committed receipt-prefix protection. The remaining Python gate and governance tests only delegate to the Rust result; no validation policy is duplicated. Static integrity is not target qualification.

Rust records validates all six original MTM-003 through MTM-008 accepted receipt identities and exact counts after baseline-bound hash validation. Original bytes and hashes remain unchanged. The redundant legacy gate invocation is removed; remaining historical governance callers consume the same Rust summary. No historical release is rerun or promoted to current qualification, and target-specific validators outside this responsibility remain pending.

The last external-binary Python caller was the now-retired MTM-015 target family. Rust capability owns current-source checks, while qualify explicitly snapshots and hashes a chosen artifact. Independent Rust tests replace the frozen Python mutation harness and require 500 normal assessments, persisted-secret restart, invalid/revoked/cross-owner handling and no blind replay. The optional historical 1-2000 sample selector is not a forward API; the current fixed 500-case gate remains mandatory. Historical harness hashes remain immutable.
verification: cargo xtask qualify --profile protocol --binary <exact candidate> --sha256 <reviewed hash> --record

Current Rust permission tests cover accept/decline/cancel and authority boundaries, record validation preserves the accepted historical receipt, and release-check still requires independently observed current browser/human evidence. Scripted consent is never promoted to human evidence.
